name: Destinee Thomas
title: Co-Founder & Creative Director (Cincinnati Art Week); Co-Founder & Principal, Cincy Nice
bio: Cultural strategist, communicator, and experience designer with a passion for helping communities feel more connected, welcoming, and alive. Destinee has led communications, partnerships, and large-scale cultural initiatives spanning public art, festivals, placemaking, and community engagement.
quote: “Cincinnati is an art city,” said Destinee Thomas, co-founder of Cincy Nice and Cincinnati Art Week. “Cincinnati Art Week is about making that identity more visible. By showcasing independent and emerging artists during one of the city’s biggest cultural moments, we’re connecting people to the creative energy that already exists while building momentum for what’s next — for artists, neighborhoods and Cincinnati as a cultural destination.”
notes: Headshot = the uncaptioned photo (1457x1235) in the "OUR TEAM" section of cincynice.com/about, placed directly under "Cincy Nice is led by co-founders Destinee and William Thomas" and above their bios; it shows two people (a shared co-founders photo, not an individual headshot). Also in the CAW team group photo: https://freight.cargo.site/t/original/i/T3056859355596179323774539701626/CINCYARTWEEK2067.png Instagram: none personal found; the organization account is @cincynice (see orgs).
quote_2: Destinee Thomas, co-founder and creative director, describes CAW as “connective tissue” for Cincinnati’s creative scene,“CAW is a platform to facilitate all of the movement within our local creative economy.”

name: William Thomas
title: Co-Founder & Partnerships Director (Cincinnati Art Week); Co-Founder & Principal, Cincy Nice
bio: Partnership builder and community strategist focused on bringing people and organizations together around ambitious ideas. William's experience spans fundraising, sponsorship development, operations, and relationship-building across cultural, civic, and neighborhood initiatives.
quote: “Cincinnati is an art city. The quality of art and artists is top tier,” he says. “There is a creative connective energy that is unique to Cincinnati.”
notes: CityBeat calls him "Billy" Thomas. Headshot = the shared co-founders photo in the "OUR TEAM" section of cincynice.com/about (two people, uncaptioned; see destinee-thomas). Also in the CAW team group photo: https://freight.cargo.site/t/original/i/T3056859355596179323774539701626/CINCYARTWEEK2067.png

title: Co-Founder & Producing Director (Cincinnati Art Week); Founder, No Standing
bio: Megyn Norbut was born to collaborate. For over a decade she has organized people, ideas, and all the moving parts needed to create intentional and meaningful events. Since founding No Standing, Megyn has built a strong reputation for producing progressive events that embody each client’s mission.

name: Javarri Lewis
title: Curatorial Advisor (Creative Collaborator); NO GRID speaker
bio: Cincinnati based Artist Javarri Lewis journey is marked by a commitment to engaging communities through art—whether through large-scale murals, digital projects, or immersive public events. Drawing inspiration from Cincinnati’s rich heritage and diverse narratives, Javarri invites viewers to pause, reflect, and rediscover the connections that shape our shared experiences. Always evolving, his art continues to serve as a powerful medium for dialogue, unity, and cultural celebration.

name: Mz. Icar
title: Artist collective — experiential art piece (Cincinnati Art Week)
bio:
Mz. Icar, an anonymous art collective predominantly comprised of Black Women, stands at the intersection of artistic innovation and societal transformation. Our collective name, “racIzM,” spelled backward, serves as a guiding principle, symbolizing our mission to upend conventional constructs of gender and race. We recognize these identifiers as fluid concepts, deeply influenced by the nuances of time, place, and context. They are not restrictions, but rather, perspectives through which we interpret the world, explore our identities, and drive our creative journey.

Our collective is an ensemble of multi-talented artists, each specializing in distinct roles within our creative process. Among us, skilled Illustrators, Photographers, Designers, Prop Stylists, Street Artists, and Collage Artists unite with a common vision. Together, we create art that celebrates the essence of Women, the global tapestry of Blackness, and the spirit of play.

Our artistic odyssey with Mz. Icar is a kaleidoscope of projects and creations. We’ve ventured into exhibitions, murals, public installations, augmented reality-activated public art, and brand collaborations, all bearing the indelible marks of play, color, composition, and a celebration of diverse narratives. Our murals span from local treasures to international marvels, infusing vibrancy and life into public spaces. Beyond this, we’ve directed an award-winning short film, “Of Expansion,” and lent our conceptual art and art direction to Ms. Lauryn Hill’s World Tour. Collaborations with renowned brands such as Doritos, BET, and Xbox have allowed us to infuse our artistic vision into various media.
notes: Cincinnati Magazine: "You might find an experiential art piece by Mz. Icar, an installation exploring identity by local architect Chas Wiederhold, or Prints and Plants, a pop-up with local artist Gee Horton." Bio = first three paragraphs of the BIOGRAPHY section on mzicar.com/info (truncated). Also a BLINK 2022/2024 artist per No Standing.

bio: Studio Ausgang is an architecture and design studio led by Chas Wiederhold, an Ohio-based architect with over a decade of experience working across residential, commercial, civic, and cultural projects.
notes: Cincinnati Magazine: "an installation exploring identity by local architect Chas Wiederhold".

name: Gee Horton
title: Artist — "Prints and Plants" pop-up (Cincinnati Art Week)
bio: Gee Horton (/dʒi ˈhɔːrtən/) is an American contemporary artist based in Cincinnati, Ohio. He is recognized for his graphite and charcoal portraiture, as well as mixed-media works that address themes of identity, memory, and emotional experience. Horton's practice often integrates photorealistic drawing with archival materials and installation, focusing on aspects of Black adolescence and masculinity.
